chapter: Leaving Duke and the Goodman sextet
title: The Goodman sextet year
summary: Duke advised him to be featured only with the sextet; it was the most relaxed and best-paid year of his career.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Yeah. So you joined the band in New York?
And you sat up there in the trumpet section.
Oh. You were there for the sextet.
Duke told me, "Only for the sextet." He said, "You'll get lost, sitting back there in the band."
So rig up the thing where you'll only be featured with the sextet.
So he drew up the contract where I was only to be featured with the sextet. Duke thought of that.
Yeah. Yeah. Well, so Georgie All was in there.
No. Lionel wasn't there. Charlie Christian.
Myself and Bennie. Who else was in --
Was that before? No Lionel had left, hadn't he?
Who was playing piano? Not Jess. Teddy.
Oh, it was one of those boys --
And was there a bass player?
Yeah. Well, I'll tell you Helen, to tell you the truth, that was the most relaxed thing that I ever had in my life in music. In job or anything I ever had in music. That year.
Well, how come? I mean, you were getting a kick out of it.

Well, yeah. I enjoyed playing. I enjoyed playing. Everybody in the sextet was great. And each man that you had to follow to play behind, you had to play. And that sextet used to romp. And there wasn't no slack there.
Nothing wrong. At all. And you had to play. And I just enjoyed it so much.
And he had to play, too.
Yeah. Yeah. Which thrilled him, because he never -- he very seldom ever had to play.
Yeah. And I just really enjoyed it, you know. And I didn't have to worry about the money or working.
It was the most money I had made in my life.
You got a check every week. And I had never been used to that.
Well, Cootie, the only thing was, you didn't get to play very much, though.
What'd you play? Three times a night? Or more?
Sometimes more. When he felt -- sometimes he kept the band off. He'd start off with the band, and then -- Friday nights, sometimes, he'd keep the sextet on.
Yeah. Sometimes that sextet would stay on an hour and a half.
Oh, well, yeah. Well, in that case, you did get enough to blow, then.
Then, sometimes, if the trumpet player wasn't there, the snag used to come in. He wanted me to set in the band.
And play. And sometimes I'd do it, you know.
I saw you up in the section. I caught the band one time, when you were sitting up there in the section. Yeah. Well, did you actually enjoy playing a few numbers with the band itself?
No, no, I enjoyed it. Enjoyed playing too with the band, But I remembered what Duke said. "Don't let him set you up there in the band."
And so you knew you weren't doing the right thing.
